item.title: Tree Affecting Driveway/Private Property, 7th September
item.description:
Dear Sir/Madam, RE: Formal Complaint and Intent to Pursue Legal Action – Property Damage and Actionable Nuisance Caused by Council-Owned Tree Location of Property: Adjacent 2A Dulverton Road Description of Tree: Mature Tree situated on council land directly adjacent to the boundary of 2A Dulverton Road. I am writing to formally lodge a complaint regarding the severe and ongoing damage being caused to my private driveway by the roots of the council-owned tree located immediately adjacent to my property boundary. Despite multiple formal reports from myself over a span of several years requesting that this tree be appropriately managed and cut back, the council has consistently failed to take effective action. Causation and Ongoing Encroachment The roots of the mature tree have heavily encroached beneath my property boundary line, resulting in localized shifting and lifting of my block-paved driveway. As a direct consequence of this root activity, the driveway surface has become significantly uneven, creating a structural hazard, breaking the joints between the pavers, and forcing the bedding material upward. Historical Notice and Foreseeability The council has long been on notice regarding this issue. Approximately ten (10) years ago, a council representative attended my property to inspect initial concerns regarding potential tree damage. At that time, the representative claimed that the tree was not the source of the issue. Subsequent years have comprehensively disproven that assessment. The tree has continued to grow completely unchecked, and the damage to my driveway has expanded exactly in line with the spread of the tree's root system. Furthermore, I have repeatedly contacted the council to report the overgrowth and requested that the canopy and roots be cut back, yet these requests have been systematically ignored. Formal Demand and Notice of Intent to Take Legal Action The ongoing encroachment of these roots onto my private land and the resulting physical destruction of my property constitutes a clear and actionable Private Nuisance under UK common law. Because the council has been aware of this risk for a decade and has repeatedly failed to execute its duty of care to maintain its property safely, the council holds full legal liability for the damage. I hereby request that the council: 1. Instruct an independent arboricultural specialist and surveyor to inspect the tree and damage within 14 days of this letter. 2. Provide a formal written commitment to repair the damaged driveway to its original condition at the council's expense. 3. Formally agree to implement a root barrier or ongoing maintenance plan to prevent recurrence. Please find attached clear photographic evidence detailing the scale of the tree, its immediate proximity to my boundary fence, and the specific structural lifting of the block pavers on my driveway. Should the council refuse to take immediate responsibility for these repairs, fail to respond within 14 days, or continue to neglect its statutory maintenance duties, I will have no alternative but to instruct my legal counsel to initiate formal court proceedings against the council without further notice. I will seek full compensation for the cost of professional driveway reinstatement, legal fees, and associated surveyor expenses. I look forward to your urgent response. Yours faithfully, Hassan Shakir Enclosures: Photographic Evidence of Tree Proximity and Driveway Damage

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 2A, Dulverton Road, New Eltham, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
